steps.title: Five steps from data to earnings

s1.title: Train
s1.body: Upload a chat-format JSONL, pick a Nemotron base model and start training. You pay for the GPU time the run actually used.
s1.assist: Only have documents? Nemotron drafts training examples from them.

s2.title: Deploy
s2.body: Your LoRA is loaded onto the base model in a vLLM endpoint. It stops on its own after {{idle}} minutes without calls.

s3.title: Test
s3.body: Check real responses in the in-browser playground.
s3.assist: Nemotron sends the same prompts to the base model and to your fine-tuned model, and compares the answers.

s4.title: Publish
s4.body: Set prices per 1M input and output tokens and per request, then publish to the store.

s5.title: Earn
s5.body: Users call your model at /v1 with their own API key. Each call credits {{share}}% of your price to your earnings.

why.title: Sell a model without running GPUs

gpu.title: No GPUs to manage
gpu.body: Training and inference run on Nebius serverless GPUs. Forkline reserves the machines and starts and stops the containers.

idle.title: Pay only while it runs
idle.body: Endpoints are billed per minute while running and stop after {{idle}} minutes without calls. A stopped endpoint costs nothing.

api.title: OpenAI-compatible API
api.body: Users change the base_url in any OpenAI SDK and call your model. Streaming is supported.

payout.title: Paid out through Stripe Connect
payout.body: Earnings add up and can be paid out through Stripe Connect from ¥{{min}}.

why.splitNote: GPU time is separate: it is deducted from the creator's credits for the time the endpoint runs.

train.detail: A PEFT + TRL container trains the LoRA on one GPU.

serve.detail: vLLM loads the base model with your LoRA and answers calls. Stops when idle.

storage.detail: Holds datasets and trained LoRA adapters (S3-compatible).

assist.detail: Calls Nemotron as-is to draft training data from your documents and to evaluate the fine-tuned model.

api.title: Works with the OpenAI SDK
api.lead: Point base_url at Forkline and set model to the model ID shown in the store.
api.prompt: How do I return an item?
api.warm: A model that hasn't been called for a while takes a few minutes to start. Until then it returns 503 with Retry-After; wait that long and send the request again.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q2: Who pays for GPU time, and when?
faq.a2: The person who builds the model. For training, the estimate is held up front and settled on the actual time. Endpoints are billed per minute while they run.
faq.q3: What happens to endpoints nobody uses?
faq.a3: They stop after {{idle}} minutes without calls, and no GPU time is billed. A call to a stopped endpoint starts it and returns 503 with Retry-After.
faq.a4: Users buy prepaid credits, and each call deducts the model's price. Each user has their own API keys and balance.
faq.q5: Does it work with the OpenAI SDK?
faq.a5: Yes. Set base_url to https://forkline.ai/v1 and model to the model ID. Streaming is supported.
faq.q6: Is my data used to train Forkline's own models?
faq.a6: No. Datasets and trained LoRA adapters are kept in Nebius Object Storage until you delete the model or your account.

docs.metaDescription: How to call Forkline's OpenAI-compatible API, and how to fine-tune and publish Nemotron: auth, streaming, pricing, errors and payouts.
docs.title: Documentation
docs.intro: Forkline's API is OpenAI-compatible. Call any published model with one API key from the same endpoint. The second half covers building and publishing your own model.
docs.placeholder: Replace your-model with the model ID shown in the store. Model IDs use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

quickstart.title: Quickstart
quickstart.body: Three steps to your first call.

steps.key: Create a key under "API keys" in the console. It is shown only once.
steps.credits: Buy credits under "Billing" (¥{{min}} to ¥{{max}} per purchase).
steps.call: Set the base URL to {{url}} and call it with an OpenAI SDK or curl.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.body: Send the API key as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. Calls are charged to the credits of the person who created the key.

chat.title: Chat completions
chat.body: Call POST /v1/chat/completions. Requests and responses have the same shape as OpenAI's Chat Completions API.

streaming.title: Streaming
streaming.body: Set stream: true to receive Server-Sent Events. The last chunk carries usage (token counts), followed by data: [DONE].

list.title: List models
list.body: GET /v1/models returns the models published in the store and your own models. id is the model ID.

pricing.title: Pricing and units
pricing.body: You pay the price the model's creator sets. The creator pays for GPU time, so the listed price is all you pay.

units.tokens: Input and output tokens are priced in yen per 1M tokens each.
units.request: Some models also charge a price per request.
units.hold: Before a call, an estimate is held from your credits; after the response it is settled on the actual token counts. If the balance is too low, the call returns 402.
units.header: The amount charged (JPY) is returned in the X-Forkline-Cost-JPY header for regular responses, and in a final SSE comment line starting with ": cost_jpy=" for streams. SSE clients ignore comment lines.
units.self: Calling your own models does not charge the price.

warmup.title: Cold starts (503)
warmup.body: A Nebius-hosted model's endpoint stops after {{idle}} minutes without calls. A call to a stopped endpoint starts it and immediately returns 503 model_warming_up with a Retry-After header ({{retry}} seconds). Starting can take a few minutes.
warmup.retry: The OpenAI SDKs retry 503 responses on their own and honour Retry-After. Raise max_retries so the client waits through a cold start.

errors.title: Errors
errors.body: Errors use the same shape as OpenAI's.
errors.invalidRequest: The request body is malformed (model and messages are required)
errors.invalidApiKey: The API key is missing, malformed or revoked
errors.insufficientCredits: The credit balance is too low
errors.modelSuspended: The model has been suspended by the operator
errors.modelNotFound: The model does not exist or is not published
errors.modelNotDeployed: The model has not been deployed to an endpoint yet
errors.rateLimit: Rate limit exceeded (600 requests per minute per API key)
errors.warmingUp: The endpoint is starting. Wait for Retry-After seconds and retry

publish.title: From dataset to store
publish.body: In the console, create a model under "Models" with "Fine-tune Nemotron" and follow these steps.

steps.dataset: Choose a training dataset (chat-format JSONL). If you only have documents, Nemotron can draft one from them.
steps.train: Pick a base model and hyperparameters and start training.
steps.deploy: When training finishes, deploy the LoRA to an endpoint.
steps.test: Check responses in the playground. Nemotron evaluates them against the base model's answers.
steps.price: Set your prices, write a summary and publish to the store.

dataset.title: Dataset format
dataset.body: Write one conversation per line as JSON. role is system, user or assistant, and content is a non-empty string.

rules.user: Each line needs at least one user turn and one assistant turn.
rules.size: Files can be up to {{mb}} MB.
rules.check: The format is checked both in the browser and on the server.

hyperparameters.title: Hyperparameters
hyperparameters.body: The defaults work for most datasets.
hyperparameters.epochs: How many passes over the dataset (1–10).
hyperparameters.loraRank: LoRA rank ({{ranks}}). Higher is more expressive and slower to train.
hyperparameters.loraAlpha: Scaling of the LoRA weights. About twice the rank is a good start.

baseModels.title: Base models and GPUs
baseModels.body: Each base model trains and serves on one GPU of the following type.

compute.title: GPU costs and idle stop
compute.body: GPU time for training and endpoints is deducted from the creator's credits.

items.train: Training: {{multiplier}}× the estimate is held at the start and settled on the actual GPU time at the end. Runs longer than {{hours}} hours are stopped.
items.endpoint: Endpoints: the boot and idle time is held when an endpoint starts, and running time is billed every minute.
items.idle: An endpoint stops {{idle}} minutes after its last call, and no GPU time is billed after that. The next call starts it again and returns 503 with Retry-After until it is ready.

payouts.title: Prices and payouts
payouts.body: Prices are set in yen, per model.

items.price: Set prices per 1M input tokens, per 1M output tokens and per request. Set them all to 0 to publish for free.
items.fee: Your earnings are the price users pay minus the platform fee ({{fee}}%), credited to your earnings.
items.payout: Once Stripe Connect onboarding is complete, you can request payouts from ¥{{min}}.
